lacuna.name: opencode-local-loop-semantics
lacuna.repo_anchor: The step subprocess is spawned by the weco local fork only. .host-software [software "weco-skill"]: 'The CLI is NOT a lane: uv tool install from the fork directly, weco 0.4.0, resolved sha 0111f27e0e370d2ccac4e06e28a6398bda48a95b' (checkout at /tmp/weco-cli-bug, upstream remote connollydavid/weco-cli, sha 0111f27 = 'start: add the minimal codex bridge'). The exact spawn chain, quoted from source: weco/commands/local_cmd.py `weco local run` builds harness_step = make_opencode_step(workdir, metric=..., maximize=...) with NO harness/agent options exposed (--harness choices=['opencode'] default 'opencode'); weco/local/loop.py make_opencode_step calls run_opencode_bridge(prompt=prompt, agent=None-or-arg, forwarded_args=[], console) and `if code != 0: raise RuntimeError(f"the opencode harness exited {code}")` - nonzero exit aborts the whole campaign, and there is NO timeout on the opencode subprocess anywhere in the chain; weco/commands/start/opencode_bridge.py run_opencode_bridge runs `argv = ["opencode", "run", "--format", "json"]` + optional ["--agent", agent] + forwarded_args + prompt, via `subprocess.Popen(argv, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=None, text=True, bufsize=1)` - argv[0] is the bare name resolved through PATH, STDIN IS INHERITED (never DEVNULL), stderr is inherited, the loop parses each stdout line as JSON (non-JSON chatter passes through), and the function returns process.wait()'s code; the harness_step prompt is 'Optimization step {n}: improve the {metric} metric ({goal}) ... The best {metric} so far is {best}; beat it. ... Edit files only; do not run the evaluation loop yourself.' - so cross-step context exists ONLY as this one best-value sentence plus the files on disk. `weco start opencode` (a different entrypoint) DOES preflight via _require_opencode_cli/shutil.which and exits 1 with 'opencode CLI not found', but make_opencode_step bypasses that check: with opencode off PATH the local loop dies with a raw FileNotFoundError from Popen. Host state verified 2026-09-11: opencode 1.18.25 at ~/.opencode/bin/opencode (reports 1.18.25), `which opencode` FAILS (exit 1) - the known PATH gap is live; ~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc sets model rope/qwen3.6-27b (context 221184/output 32768) with apiKey "{env:ROPE_BEARER}", 5 MCP servers (incl. zai-mcp-server via `npx -y` - a network fetch on cold cache), plugin @bybrawe/opencode-goal@1.3.16, lsp:true; ROPE_BEARER is not exported into non-login shells; sessions persist in ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db (SQLite, 131 MB on this host). MEMORY.md 2026-09-08 (weco near-miss) pins the posture: 'this host's weco is the LOCAL-ONLY FORK (connollydavid/weco-cli@0111f27e per .host-software; local mode is the DEFAULT per the skill's own local-mode.md: no login, no credits, no endpoints)'; ~/.zcode/skills/weco/references/local-mode.md: 'The configured agent harness (opencode) improves the code each step; the eval command measures it; the best result and every step land in .weco/local-loop/' and 'Local mode makes no outbound connections' (true of the weco CLI itself, NOT of the opencode subprocess it spawns, which talks to the rope provider endpoint by design).
lacuna.current_status: Upstream opencode (github.com/anomalyco/opencode, formerly sst/opencode; docs at opencode.ai) releases near-daily: v1.18.30 on 2026-09-09 is latest, the host's v1.18.25 shipped 2026-08-28 (Azure-auth patch). THE RUN CONTRACT (verified against the local 1.18.25 binary --help plus packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/run.ts at master, Sept 2026): `opencode run [message..]` is non-interactive by design ('sends a single prompt, streams events to stdout, and exits when the session goes idle'); flags: -c/--continue 'continue the last session', -s/--session <id> 'session id to continue' (unknown id -> exit 1 'Session not found'), --fork (copy before continuing, requires -c/-s; misuse -> exit 1, verified locally), --agent (unknown or subagent name -> warning + fallback to default agent), -m/--model provider/model, --command (slash-command with message as args), -f/--file (<=10 MiB), --title, --share, --format default|json ('raw JSON events'), --attach http://host:port (run against a persistent `opencode serve`), --dir, --port (in-process server on a RANDOM port when not attaching), --variant, --thinking, --auto 'auto-approve permissions that are not explicitly denied (dangerous!)' (hidden aliases --yolo, --dangerously-skip-permissions), global --print-logs/--log-level/--pure (no external plugins). SESSION/STATE MODEL: default = a FRESH session created per invocation (sdk.session.create); --continue resumes the most recent non-parent session from session.list(); sessions are per-directory (the instance boots for the run's directory), persisted in ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db, manageable via `opencode session list|delete` and `opencode export [sessionID]`; there is NO built-in session flag in the weco bridge, so every local-loop step is fresh context: AGENTS.md (project root found by upward traversal; CLAUDE.md fallback; global ~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md) + instructions array from config + the one-shot prompt + whatever the files on disk say. PERMISSIONS IN RUN MODE: the session is created with bootstrap rules denying question, plan_enter, plan_exit; per the permissions docs most tools (read, edit, glob, grep, bash, task, webfetch...) DEFAULT TO 'allow' (exceptions: doom_loop and external_directory 'ask'; .env reads denied), config permission blocks (ask/allow/deny, wildcard patterns, last-match-wins, OPENCODE_PERMISSION inline JSON) apply, and on a permission.asked event run mode AUTO-REJECTS with a warning unless --auto is set (reply 'once' then) - this landed with PR #11814 'cli: make run non-interactive' (merged 2026-02-03, closing #10411); before that, 'ask' rules HUNG run mode (#3503, and #11899 question-tool hang). EXIT CODES as of 1.18.25: usage errors exit 1 (verified: no message, --fork misuse); provider/API failure -> session.error path -> a JSON error event AND exit 1 (VERIFIED locally: with ROPE_BEARER unset the rope endpoint returned 401 and opencode emitted {"type":"error","timestamp":<ms>,"sessionID":"ses_...","error":{"name":"APIError","data":{"message":"Unauthorized...","statusCode":401,"isRetryable":false,...}}} then exit=1; the message even suggests `opencode auth login <provider URL>` - run mode never prompts for auth, it errors). History of exit-code holes: #2489 (exit 0 despite errors), #15558 (invalid model: stderr error, exit 0), #14551 (session errors left exit 0 because the event loop was never awaited; closed not-planned as compliance-bot process, but current master awaits the loop and maps accumulated errors to exitCode 1), #27870 (v1.15.x, May 2026: run exits 0 with ZERO stdout while the agent silently executes - 'breaks all programmatic/CI usage'; closed with no visible fix) [uncertain: opencode-zero-stdout-on-1.18.25]. STDIN (the sharpest edge): when stdin is not a TTY, run.ts reads ALL of stdin (`await Bun.stdin.text()`) and APPENDS it to the message - an EOF-less pipe blocks forever; reproduced locally on 1.18.25 (`sleep 60 | timeout 12 opencode run ... --format json` -> killed at 12s, exit 124) and reported upstream as #11891 (2026-02-03, Popen hang 'indefinitely on first read'; first JSON line `type=step_start` arrives ~7s in a terminal). The --format json stream (master run.ts emit()): one JSON object per line {type, timestamp: epoch-ms, sessionID, ...} with types step_start, step_finish, tool_use (tool part completed/error), text (assistant text part), reasoning (only with --thinking), error [uncertain: opencode-json-event-set-1.18.25 - error/step_start confirmed, full set inferred from master + #11891]; note these are NOT the server SSE names (message.updated etc.) the fork's bridge fixtures were pinned against - normalize_event still works (sessionID extracted from every line, text extracted from part.type=='text', unknown kinds pass through under data). TIMEOUTS: there is NO timeout flag and no idle watchdog; the event loop only breaks on session.status=idle, so a tool that never returns or a wedged stream hangs the process forever (#17516, v1.2.26, 2026-03-14: 'hangs after completing tool calls - process never exits', closed not-planned; the reporter was driving opencode run from a CLI optimization loop 'ratchet' - our exact pattern). ENVIRONMENT/PERFORMANCE: every invocation boots an in-process server (config chain: global opencode.json -> OPENCODE_CONFIG -> project opencode.json[c] up to git root -> OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT, with {env:}/{file:} placeholder substitution) plus all MCP servers (cold npx fetch risk), LSP, and plugins (~7s cold start per #11891) - the CLI docs explicitly recommend `opencode serve` + `run --attach` 'to avoid MCP server cold boot times on every run'; relevant env: OPENCODE_PERMISSION, OPENCODE_CONFIG*, OPENCODE_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE, OPENCODE_DISABLE_PRUNE, OPENCODE_DISABLE_MODELS_FETCH, OPENCODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_CODE [uncertain: opencode-autoupdate-in-run-mode - whether background self-update can swap the binary under a long campaign; the kill switch exists and should be set regardless]. CI-pipeline history: #13851 (v1.1.60, 2026-02-16) claims the bootstrap permission preset overrode config and neutered write/edit in run mode (closed as bug, no visible fix note) - the modern rules array denies only question/plan_* so headless edit/bash work again; #10411/#11814 established the intended contract: 'in non-interactive mode, a permission question should just abort the session and exit'.
lacuna.applicability: Direct answers for the weco-local runner. WHAT ONE STEP GETS TODAY: a fresh opencode process AND a fresh session (no -c/-s forwarded by the bridge), running in the weco process's cwd (the bridge does not even pass --dir; make_opencode_step relies on the loop being launched from workdir); the model is the global-config default rope/qwen3.6-27b (no -m passed); context = workdir AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md + config instructions + the one-line best-value prompt + the files themselves; the ONLY guarantees returned are (a) exit code 0/1 and (b) a normalized JSONL stream on weco's stdout (of which make_opencode_step uses only the exit code - the assistant text, error events, and sessionID are logged, never parsed); cross-step memory is exclusively the filesystem and the best-value number. WHAT UPSTREAM OFFERS THAT THE FORK DOES NOT USE: -c/-s/--fork session chaining (sessions are durable in SQLite per directory, so a step could resume the prior step's ses_ id for accumulated context - a real optimization-dynamics decision: fresh exploration vs growing context/cost), --attach against a persistent `opencode serve` to kill the ~7s-per-step cold boot and the npx/MCP network fetch, --auto or a project opencode.json permission block to stop silent auto-rejects, --print-logs for stderr diagnostics, --command for prompt-template-style steps, --pure to skip the host's plugin. WHAT BREAKS A STEP, WITH LOCAL PROOF: (1) STDIN - if weco local runs where stdin is a non-TTY open pipe, EVERY step hangs forever (reproduced: exit 124 after 12s kill; matches #11891); the fix is one token: stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL in run_opencode_bridge; never launch the loop inside a pipeline. (2) PATH - argv[0] is bare 'opencode'; on this host ~/.opencode/bin is not on PATH (verified), so the first step raises FileNotFoundError and the campaign dies; fix at wrapper level (absolute binary path from config) or environment (export PATH). (3) AUTH/ENV - ROPE_BEARER missing -> clean failure (401 error event + exit 1, verified), so make_opencode_step's RuntimeError DOES catch it, but the campaign still aborts on step one - a preflight check belongs in the runner, not after spawn. (4) PERMISSIONS - an 'ask' permission is auto-rejected with a warning the loop never surfaces; defaults allow edit/bash so normal steps work, but doom_loop/external_directory and any project config 'ask' silently cap the agent; encode the intended policy in a per-workdir opencode.json (allow edit within workdir, explicit bash allowlist/denylist) instead of --auto, which would also approve the dangerous rest. (5) HANGS WITH NO EXIT - the run loop breaks only on idle (#17516 unfixed), a wedged provider stream or MCP boot can park a step indefinitely; no internal timeout exists, so the external per-step timeout from the unattended-loop-supervision item is the only defense - this item supplies its target process-group shape (opencode spawns children; kill the group). (6) SILENT SUCCESS - exit-0-with-zero-output class (#27870, #15558): treat 'no assistant text event and no error event' as a failed/skipped step, because exit code alone is not a sufficient success predicate on this stack. (7) VERSION DRIFT - the fork's test fixtures pin old server-shaped events (session.id, message.updated, message.part.updated) while 1.18.x emits step_start/text/tool_use/error (error shape verified locally); passthrough keeps the bridge functional but any future assertion on envelope.session_id should read sessionID off every line (normalize_event already does); pin the binary version in doctrine (OPENCODE_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE=1) so a 5-releases-per-week upstream cannot change step semantics mid-campaign. DOES NOT TRANSFER: TUI-only surfaces (plan mode, --mini/--interactive, share UI), `opencode attach` (no message/batch flags per #13851), github/pr subcommands, the models.dev catalog fetch (local provider config is self-contained), and claude-code rule fallbacks (this host has no ~/.claude on the loop path).

design.mechanism: The hardened step contract, implementable cold in the fork (weco/local/loop.py + weco/commands/start/opencode_bridge.py). (A) Spawn: resolve the binary ONCE from config/env (WECO_OPENCODE_BIN or shutil.which, else fail with the friendly 'opencode CLI not found' message the start command already has - make_opencode_step must not bypass it); argv = [opencode_bin, 'run', '--format', 'json', *( ['--agent', agent] if agent else [] ), prompt]; Popen(..., stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE or inherited, text=True, bufsize=1, start_new_session=True for group-kill). (B) Success predicate: step ok IFF exit code == 0 AND the normalized stream contained at least one assistant text part (envelope.text from a text event) - this covers the #27870/#15558 exit-0-but-dead class; on nonzero exit OR empty-output, retry per the supervision policy, never `raise RuntimeError` directly. (C) Telemetry: parse the {type:'error'} events (name/statusCode/message at error.data.message - shape verified on 1.18.25) into the step's steps.jsonl entry {status, exit, error_message, session_id}; the sessionID is on every JSON line, so record it - it is the resume key. (D) Optional session chaining (operator decision, off by default): pass ['--session', last_session_id] (or --continue) so step N+1 inherits step N's context instead of rebuilding from files; --fork variant for branching experiments; cost grows with context, and 221k-token qwen3.6-27b headroom makes ~5-10 chained steps safe before compaction concerns. (E) Permission posture: a committed opencode.json in the workdir (or OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT) with permission {"*":"allow","bash":{"git *":"allow","...": allowlist},"edit":"allow"} rather than --auto; explicit deny for paths outside workdir; never forward --auto blindly. (F) Preflight (wrapper, before step 1): binary found + `--version` equals the pinned string, ROPE_BEARER non-empty (config substitution fails closed at the provider otherwise - verified 401), one 1-line `run --format json 'reply pong'` smoke step against the real provider, OPENCODE_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE=1 exported. (G) Optional performance variant: `opencode serve --port 4096` as a supervised sidecar and steps via --attach http://localhost:4096 --dir <workdir> to amortize the ~7s MCP/LSP/plugin cold boot - only if step cadence makes it worth a second supervised process.
design.failure_modes: Documented and locally reproduced: (1) stdin inheritance hang - non-TTY stdin is read to EOF and joined into the message (run.ts Bun.stdin.text()); an EOF-less pipe hangs every step forever (reproduced exit 124; upstream #11891); defense: stdin=DEVNULL, plus never run the loop mid-pipeline. (2) No internal timeout - run exits only on session idle; hung tool or wedged stream parks the process (#17516, closed not-planned); defense: external process-group TERM/KILL from the loop supervisor (opencode spawns bash/edit children - kill the group, not the pid). (3) Exit-0 lies - invalid model or zero-stdout runs exit 0 (#15558, #27870), so a code-only check marks dead steps successful; defense: require an assistant text event. (4) Silent auto-reject - permission.asked is auto-rejected in run mode (by design post-#11814) with only a stdout warning the loop discards; a step whose needed tool was denied 'succeeds' with no edits - the next eval then measures stale code and may 'confirm' a bogus no-change best; defense: surface 'permission requested ... auto-rejecting' lines into the step record, and pre-authorize via config allow-rules. (5) Question/plan tools denied at bootstrap (#13851 history) - any prompt style that relies on asking the user degrades silently; defense: doctrine - prompts must be self-contained (the fork's step prompt already is). (6) PATH/env drift - bare argv[0] plus an env-var API key means the loop is coupled to the launching shell's PATH and ROPE_BEARER (both verified fragile on this host); defense: preflight + absolute path + explicit env. (7) Cold-boot cost and network - each step re-boots 5 MCP servers (one via npx -y, a network fetch on cold cache), LSP, and a plugin (~7s, #11891); a provider outage mid-campaign yields 401 error events + exit 1 (verified) - retryable, isRetryable:false in the observed payload; defense: bounded retry, or --attach to a persistent serve. (8) Upstream churn - near-daily releases (v1.18.24..30 within 12 days) and event-shape drift (fork fixtures pin server SSE names, 1.18.x emits step_start/text/tool_use/error); defense: version pin + OPENCODE_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE=1 + the passthrough normalization that already tolerates unknown types; re-pin deliberately. (9) Session db growth (131 MB opencode.db on this host) with fresh sessions created per step forever - pruning is on by default (OPENCODE_DISABLE_PRUNE off) but unbounded step counts mean unbounded db growth and per-step session.list() cost under --continue; defense: campaign-length bound or periodic session delete.
design.effort_estimate: Fork-level (weco-cli, small patches on the 0111f27 base): stdin=DEVNULL + start_new_session + absolute-binary resolution in run_opencode_bridge (~10 lines); success-predicate + error-event parsing + RuntimeError removal in make_opencode_step (~25 lines); optional --session chaining flag through local_cmd (~15 lines). Wrapper-level (tools/campaign-runner): preflight (binary, version pin, ROPE_BEARER, provider smoke step) + committed per-workdir opencode.json permission template (~40 lines shell/Python + one JSON file). Doctrine-only: runbook entry (PATH/ROPE_BEARER/OPENCODE_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE requirements, never-pipeline-the-loop rule, pinned version, the permission allowlist).
design.priority_signal: For: this subprocess is the campaign's entire intelligence source, and on this host's exact binary two of its failure classes are ALREADY reproduced (stdin hang exit 124; missing-auth 401 exit 1) while a third (opencode off PATH) makes the very first step crash today - no other lacuna in this research has live, host-verified breakage of the loop's core primitive. The upstream contract is unusually well-documented in source (run.ts is readable end-to-end: exit paths, permission auto-reject, idle-break, stdin join) and the fixes are tiny (DEVNULL is one argument). Against: the supervision consequences (timeout, retry, skip-and-continue, watchdog) are owned by the unattended-loop-supervision item - this item should land only the contract fixes (spawn hygiene, success predicate, preflight, permission posture, version pin) and hand the hang/abort handling upward; session chaining is an optimization-dynamics experiment (fresh context per step is a defensible default for mutation-style optimization, and chaining multiplies token cost per step), so it should be an explicit flag, not the default; --attach/serve amortization adds a second supervised process and is not worth it until step cadence is measured.
